name: Kwaio
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: Stress within morphemes is, with few exceptions, placed on the penultimate vowel. Stress is somewhat heavier on the penultimate vowel of the final segment of a polymorphemic form.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict penultimate, rule 10/010/0010..) rests on the only reference grammar of Kwaio, Keesing 1985 PL B-88, which we hold in full; the deciding quotation was confirmed verbatim at printed p. 9 section 1.2.2 (p. 17), with the supporting p. 11-12 and p. 20 statements also present. Keesing treats each vowel as a syllable (CVV 'technically bisyllabic', p. 9-10), so 'penultimate vowel' maps cleanly onto penultimate-syllable stress; the listed exceptions (CVV verb + monosyllabic object suffix; a handful of unanalyzable trisyllabic bases) are lexically/morphologically limited and already noted in the record's source text, so fixed-strict with the existing note is defensible. Glottolog lists no other grammatical or phonological description; the 1975 dictionary (downloaded now from the open PL archive) is silent on stress placement.
